exact_alert.finding: In cor-q-is-meager-and-not-g-delta, the second Remark says 'Uncountability and being residual are independent properties'. For subsets of ℝ this is false: every residual set is uncountable. If a residual set S were countable, S would be meager by its enumeration into nowhere dense singletons, while ℝ∖S is meager by residuality. Their union ℝ would then be meager, contradicting thm-baire-category-r. The displayed examples establish that an uncountable set need not be residual, but cannot establish independence in both directions.
